newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures head higher.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures head higher.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures looked set for more gains after making a healthy start on the back of the Dow's overnight rise and remaining firmly established in positive territory by midday on Tuesday.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract was off its peak of 20,420 but up 175 points to 20,290 by midday. Volume was a relatively light 6,505 lots.

"The whole medium-term resistance band of 20,200-20,300 has been taken out this morning. The market has formed a bottom and it's building the momentum for a longer move upwards," a trader at a local institution said.
He said there appeared to be more Japanese institutional buying of Tokyo stocks.
"If the Japanese themselves can push the market up, that's better than if the foreigners do it because it would be more broad-based buying and less subject to the dollar/yen," he said.
He said 20,000 represented a critical support level now and the June Nikkei was likely to face some resistance around 20,500 as it headed higher.
The May MSCI Taiwan index contract was at 329.5 at 0255 GMT against its opening 328.0 on volume of 950 lots.
